Synopsis:
Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim is reinstating higher fuel subsidy quotas (RON95 petrol to 300L/month, diesel to 400L/month per eligible user), effective September 1, reversing cuts made earlier in 2026 amid elevated crude prices driven by the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran. The package also includes school funding, digital health, SME micro-financing, and an AI program for youth. The measures are politically motivated, responding to declining coalition support ahead of a general election due by early 2028.
